_meta.purpose: Complete modules of a multi-step flow. Each pattern carries its own selection metadata (intent / whenToUse / cardinality / alternatives) — there is no separate sections file.
_meta.levels: level "section" brings its own Section wrapper and is placed by a template slot. level "module" is embeddable inside another pattern and is reached via $ref.

process.stepper-section.intent: Show where the user is in the flow and which steps are done.
process.stepper-section.whenToUse: The flow has named steps the user should recognize. Prefer this over the bare progress bar whenever the steps have meaningful titles.

process.progress-section.purpose: Section holding a step counter and a determinate progress bar.
process.progress-section.intent: Show how far the user has come without naming the steps.
process.progress-section.whenToUse: The flow has many steps, or the step names carry no meaning for the user. Note the progress component offers only 25, 50 and 75 percent.

process.step.purpose: The current step: heading pair above the step's own content.
process.step.intent: Ask for exactly what this step needs.
process.step.whenToUse: Every step frame has one of these. Fill the content column with the fields, options or summary this step is about — reuse the form page-type blocks for input controls.

process.confirmation.purpose: Closing confirmation screen with a success message and one action.
process.confirmation.intent: Confirm that the flow completed and offer the single follow-up action.
process.confirmation.whenToUse: The last frame of the flow, instead of a step. It carries no Back/Next row — its own Brand button is the only action.

process.navigation-section.intent: Let the user move one step back or forward.
process.navigation-section.whenToUse: Every step frame that HAS a previous step. Back is ghost, Next is the frame's single Brand action. On the first step use process.navigation-first-section instead.

process.navigation-first-section.purpose: Section holding the first step's single, right-aligned Next action.
process.navigation-first-section.intent: Move forward from the first step, where there is nothing to go back to.
process.navigation-first-section.whenToUse: The FIRST step frame of a flow. `Zurück` is dropped, so the row holds ONE action — and a single action is right-aligned, never spread (spread with one child renders it flush left).
